title: How to Use Windows Voice Typing (Win+H) in 2026
summary: Press Win+H to dictate into any text box on Windows. Setup, commands, Fluid Dictation on Copilot+ PCs, Voice Access vs Voice Typing, and when a system-wide layer helps.
body_markdown:
## Fluid Dictation on Copilot+ PCs


On supported **Copilot+ PCs**, Microsoft documents **Fluid Dictation**: Voice Typing can correct grammar, punctuation, and filler words as you speak, using on-device small language models. Microsoft notes it is available in English locales on those devices, enabled by default once the required models finish downloading, and turned off automatically in secure fields like password boxes.\[1\]


If the Fluid Dictation toggle looks dimmed, wait for the model download (Windows Update / the teaching tip on first launch) or check Settings → Windows Update. Say **"Revert"** / **"Undo that"** (or press Ctrl+Z) if a cleanup over-edits a sentence you liked.


This is hardware- and rollout-dependent. If you are not on a Copilot+ PC, skip this section—standard Voice Typing still works without it.
